'''''Pinus balfouriana''''', the '''foxtail pine''', is a rare high-elevation [[pine]] that is [[endemic]] to [[California]], United States. It is closely related to the [[Great Basin bristlecone pine|Great Basin]] and [[Rocky Mountain bristlecone pine]]s, in the subsection ''[[Balfourianae]]''. 

== Description ==
''P. balfouriana'' is a [[tree]] to {{convert|10|-|20|m|ft|-1|abbr=on}} tall, exceptionally {{convert|35|m|ft|abbr=on}}, with a [[trunk (botany)|trunk]] up to {{convert|2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} across. Its [[leaf|leaves]] are [[needle (botany)|needle-like]], in bundles of five (or sometimes four, in the southern [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra]]) with a semi-persistent basal sheath, and {{convert|2|-|4|cm|in|frac=2|abbr=on}} long, deep glossy green on the outer face, and white on the inner faces; they persist for 10–15 years. The [[Conifer cone|cones]] are {{convert|6|–|11|cm|in|frac=2|abbr=on}} long, dark purple ripening red-brown, with soft, flexible scales each with a {{convert|1|mm|in|frac=16|adj=on|abbr=off|sp=us}} central prickle.

== Distribution ==
''P. balfouriana'' occurs in the [[subalpine zone|subalpine]] forest at an elevation of {{convert|1950|-|2750|m|ft|abbr=on}} in the [[Klamath Mountains]], and at {{convert|2300|-|3500|m|ft|abbr=on}} in the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra Nevada]]. In the Sierra Nevada, Foxtail pines are limited to the area around [[Sequoia National Park|Sequoia]] and [[Kings Canyon National Park]]s. In both areas, it is often a [[tree line]] species.

== Age ==
It is thought that ''P. balfouriana'' can live up to 3000 years in the Sierra Nevada, although the highest currently proven age is 2110 years. In the Klamath Mountains, ages are only known to about 1000 years.

== Related species ==
''P. balfouriana'' is closely related to the [[bristlecone pine]]s, being classified in the same subsection ''[[Bristlecone pine|Balfourianae]]''; it has been hybridised with the [[Pinus longaeva|Great Basin Bristlecone Pine]] in cultivation, though no hybrids have ever been found in the wild.
